long_biography.plain_text:
Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan was born in Abu Dhabi and is a son of Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan, founder of the United Arab Emirates. He entered public service through his father's office and later rose to become UAE Vice President, Deputy Prime Minister and Chairman of the Presidential Court. His career also includes chairmanships of major public investment institutions.

His clearest documented private business interest is football. Newton Investment and Development, which City Football Group says is fully owned by Sheikh Mansour, holds a majority stake in CFG, the private owner and operator of clubs across five continents. Manchester City was acquired by Sheikh Mansour in 2008 and has since become one of world football's leading clubs. His EIA and Mubadala chairmanships are public stewardship roles: both institutions identify their assets as sovereign or government-owned, not his personal property.
